001.steps:
1. Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN.
  2.Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server.
   3)Repeat all above steps on all zone types except WLAN and wireless custom zone.
001.title: At least one DHCPv6 interface can support DHCPv6 PD
001.result: in step 2, PD can be enabled and the acquired PD should be shown in Protocol Tab.

002.steps:
1. Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN.
  2.Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server.
   3)Switch to "Protocol" tab, check the info under "Delegated Prefixes Acquired via DHCPv6" table.
002.title: DHCPv6 PD info MUST be displayed in ¡°Protocol¡± tab when PD is enabled on that interface
002.result: step 3,the acquired PD display correctly in Protocol tab, the values should be same as what be set in DHCPv6 server

003.steps:
1. Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN.
  2.Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server.
   3)Switch to "Protocol" tab, check the info under "Delegated Prefixes Acquired via DHCPv6" table.
003.title: The PD information of the interface MUST be displayed, including IAID, Type, IPv6 Prefix, Prefix Length, and Lease Expires
003.result: step 3,the acquired PD info display correctly in Protocol tab, including IAID, Type, IPv6 Prefix, Prefix Length, and Lease Expires, the values should be same as what be set in DHCPv6 server.

006.steps: "1. Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN.\n  2.Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server.\n   3)Navigate to Network->Address Objects, an IPv6 AO with Network type of PD prefix for the interface that PD is enabled will be auto added.

007.steps:
1) Configure a new interface X2 , zone: LAN/DMZ/WAN¡­
2) Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server;
3) Disable PD on this new interface X2, check Address Object table, that auto added related PD AO must be deleted.
007.title: The related Delegated Prefix AO MUST be deleted when DHCPv6 PD is disabled on that interface
007.result: in step 3, when PD was disabled, the related PD AO must be deleted from Address Objects table.

008.steps:
1) Configure a new interface X2 , zone: LAN/DMZ/WAN¡­
2) Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server;
3) Disable PD on this new interface X2, check Address Object table, that auto added related PD AO must be deleted;
4) Navigate to Network->Routing, previously auto added PD related routes should be deleted.
008.title: All the related routes MUST be deleted when the related Delegated Prefix AO is deleted
008.result: in step 4, the auto added route: dst: X2 PD, interface: Drop_TunnelIf,metric:255, this route will be deleted.

009.steps: "1. Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN.\n  2.Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server.\n   3)Navigate to Network->Routing, an IPv6 route for delegated prefix destined to Drop_TunnelIf MUST be created.
009.title: An IPv6 route for delegated prefix destined to Drop_TunnelIf MUST be created
009.result: when PD is enabled, an IPv6 route  dst: X2 PD, interface: Drop_TunnelIf,metric:255, MUST be created.

010.steps:
"1. Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN.\n  2.Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server.\n   3)Configure a LAN/DMZ interface X3, switch to Advanced tab, click the "add address" button.
    4)Click the radio button"Add Downstream IPv6 Address Delegated from DHCP-PD" , choose one of DHCPv6 delegated prefix from the drop-down list(e.g.: X2 delegated prefix), then set the preferred IPv6 address, set the preferred prefix length.
010.title: Downstream interface can add IPv6 addresses based on the PD prefix
010.result:
in step 4, X3 can add IPv6 addresses based on DHCPv6 delegated prefix, the final address will firstly use DHCPv6 delegated prefix, the remaining part will make most use of the input.
E.g. X2 PD prefix is 8000:8000:8002::/48 , and user input the preferred IPv6 address as ::3:3:3:3:3/64, then finally, X3 interface IPv6 address will be 8000:8000:8002:3:3:3:3:3/64.

011.steps:
"1. Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN.\n  2.Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server.\n   3)Configure a LAN/DMZ interface X3, switch to Advanced tab, click the "add address" button.
    4)Click the radio button"Add Downstream IPv6 Address Delegated from DHCP-PD" , choose one of DHCPv6 delegated prefix from the drop-down list(e.g. X2 delegated prefix), then set the preferred IPv6 address, set the preferred prefix length:e.g. 64. <span>and if X2 PD length is 50, and the preferred prefix length is 48 , and finally , the X3 IPv6 address's prefix length will be 50.
011.title: The downstream delegated IPv6 address should choose the longer prefix length between the PD prefix length and the preferred prefix length
011.result: in step 4, X3 interface IPv6 address's prefix length should be 64, and if X2 PD length is 50, and the preferred prefix length is 48 , and finally , the X3 IPv6 address's prefix length will be 50.

012.steps:
1) Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN¡­
2) Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server;
3) Enable debug DHCPv6 on server;
4) Switch to "Protocol" tab, click "Release" button under DHCPv6 PD table to clear the already acquired PD;
5) Click "Renew" button , make sure it can acquire PD again.
012.title: When clicking Renew button, the interface should do Solicit process before getting a PD prefix
012.result: in step 5, check the server debug info, before X2 get another PD, it should send "solicit" message first.

013.steps:
1) Configure a new interface X2 , zone: LAN/DMZ/WAN¡­
2) Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server;
3) Enable dhcpv6 debug on server;
4) Switch to "Protocol" tab, click "Renew" button under DHCPv6 PD table;
013.title: When clicking Renew button, the interface should do Renew process while a PD prefix has been learned
013.result: in step 4, as X2 has already learned a PD, so it should send a "Renew" message directly to the server to extend the valid and preferred lifetimes for the addresses associated with an IA.

015.steps:
1) Configure a new interface X2 , zone: LAN/DMZ/WAN¡­
2) Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server;
3) Enable debug on DHCPv6 server;
4) Switch to "Protocol" tab, click "Release" button under DHCPv6 PD table to release the already acquired PD;
5) After clicking release button , check the PD table in Protocol Tab.
015.title: When clicking Release button, the interface MUST do Release process while a PD prefix has already been learned
015.result:
in step 4, when clicking Release button, the interface must do Release process, send Release message to server, from the debug information ,server has received the release message from DUT.
In step 5, the previously acquired PD prefix has been cleared from PD table.

016.steps:
1) Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN¡­
2) Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server;
3) Check Address Object table, there should update X2 Delegated Prefix with the acquired PD e.g. 8000:8000:8002::/48
4) Switch to "Protocol" tab, click "Release" button under DHCPv6 PD table to clear the already acquired PD;
5) After PD prefix released, navigate to Network->Address Object page, check the related AO of X2, it must be reset to a default value, like ffff:ffff::2/128
016.title: When the interface PD prefix is released, the related AO of that interface MUST be reset
016.result: in step 5, after PD prefix was released, the related AO of that interface must be reset to a default value, such as interface X2 delegated prefix AO reset to :ffff:ffff::2/128.

017.steps:
1) Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN¡­
2) Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server;
3) Configure a LAN/DMZ interface X3, switch to Advanced tab, click the "add address" button;
4) Click the radio button"Add Downstream IPv6 Address Delegated from DHCP-PD" , choose one of DHCPv6 delegated prefix from the drop-down list(ps: X2 delegated prefix), then set the preferred IPv6 address, set the preferred prefix length, then check the checkbox"Advertise Subnet Prefix of the IPv6 Address";
5) Connect a PC to X3, enable Router Advertisement on interface X3, enable packet capture on PC ;
6) Click interface X2's edit button ,switch to "Protocol" tab, click the "Release" button to release the acquired PD prefix;
7) After PD prefix released, check packets received on PC, X3 must stop advertising related subnet prefix in RA.
017.title: When the interface PD prefix is released, all related downstream interfaces MUST stop advertising related subnet prefixes
017.result: in step 7, check packets captured on PC, after X2 PD prefix released, LAN X3 interface must stop advertising related subnet prefix in RA

018.steps:
1) Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN¡­
2) Edit this interface in IPv6 interface page, select the ip-assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a DHCPv6 server, make sure it can acquire PD from this server;
3) Configure a LAN/DMZ interface X3, switch to Advanced tab, click the "add address" button;
4) Click the radio button"Add Downstream IPv6 Address Delegated from DHCP-PD" , choose one of DHCPv6 delegated prefix from the drop-down list(ps: X2 delegated prefix), then set the preferred IPv6 address, set the preferred prefix length, it will generate an IPv6 address with type "PD" and display this address on IPv6 interface page;
5) Click interface X2's edit button ,switch to "Protocol" tab, click the "Release" button to release the acquired PD prefix;
6) After PD prefix released, check interface page, LAN interface X3's PD IPv6 address will disappear from GUI.
018.title: When the PD prefix AO is reset, all related downstream interface PD addresses MUST be deleted
018.result: in step 6, After PD prefix released, check interface page, LAN interface X3's PD IPv6 address will disappear from GUI.

019.title: When the PD prefix is updated, the related PD AO MUST be updated
019.result:
step 5,when PD prefix updated, the related AO must be updated too.e.g.change PD prefix from 8000:8000:8000:: to 9000:9000:9000:: in server, and after PD prefix updated in DUT, the AO X2 Delegated Prefix will updated to  9000:9000:9000::/48
step 6,result is same as step 5.

020.title: When the PD AO is updated, all related downstream interface addresses MUST be updated
020.result:
step 7,check address object X2 delegated prefix, its value must be updated.
step 8,Check the downstream interface X3's IPv6 address, it must be updated according to the new PD prefix.
step 9,the result should be same as step 7 and step 8.

021.title: When the PD AO is updated, all related routes MUST be updated
021.result:
step 5,when PD AO is updated, all related routes must be updated. E.g.an IPv6 route  dst: X2 PD, interface: Drop_TunnelIf,metric:255, here, the destination X2 PD must be same with the new X2 PD prefix;
step 6,result is same as step 5.

022.title: When the PD AO is updated, all related downstream interface MUST update its related prefixes when sending Router Advertisements
022.result:
step 8,After PD prefix updated, check packets received on PC, X3 must advertise its subnet prefix in RA according to the new PD prefix.
step 9,the expected result is same as step 8.

023.title: DUT MUST support to enable DHCPv6 PD on physical interface
023.result:
in step 2, DUT MUST support to enable DHCPv6 PD on physical interface and can acquire PD from DHCPv6 server.
   in step 3, result should be same as step 2.

024.title: DUT MUST support to enable DHCPv6 PD when interface is in PPPoE mode
024.result: in step 2, DUT MUST support to enable DHCPv6 PD on VLAN interface and can acquire PD from DHCPv6 server.

025.steps:
1) Configure a new interface X2 , zone: WAN, select its ip-assignment as PPPoE;
  2) Switch to IPv6 interface page, edit interface X2, select PPPoEv6 address Assignment as DHCPv6, enable PD, connect it to a PPPoEv6 server(this server must support DHCPv6 and DHCPv6 PD), make sure the PPP link can be established and X2 can acquire DHCPv6 PD from this server;
025.title: DUT MUST support to enable DHCPv6 PD when interface is in PPPoE mode
025.result: in step 2, DUT MUST support to enable DHCPv6 PD when interface is in PPPoE mode and can acquire PD from DHCPv6 server.

051.title: DHCPv6 PD information MUST be contained in TSR when PD is enabled on one interface
051.result: in step 3, DHCPv6 PD information MUST be contained in TSR when PD is enabled on one interface

052.initial: DHCPv6 PD information MUST be contained in TSR when PD is enabled on one interface
052.title: Enable DHCPv6 PD on some interfaces (physical, or VLAN), export prefs and import again, then reboot, the DHCPv6 PD settings MUST remain the same
052.result: in step 3,Enable DHCPv6 PD on some interfaces (physical, or VLAN or PPPoE mode), export prefs and import again, then reboot, the DHCPv6 PD settings MUST remain the same as before.

101.steps:
Part A: IA_PD Option Format
    1. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT.
    2. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.
Part B: Server identifier Option Format
    3. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT.
    4. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.
    5. Upon the reception of a Solicit message from the NUT, TN1 transmits a valid Advertise message including a Server Identifier Option.
    6. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.
Part C: IA_PD Prefix Option Format
    7. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT
    8. Upon reception of a Solicit message from the NUT, TR1 transmits a properly formatted Advertise message including an IA_PD option with a Prefix option.
    9. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.
Part D: IAID Consistency
    10. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT
    11. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.
    12. Reboot NUT
    13. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT
    14. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.
101.title: To verify that the requesting router transmits the correct prefix options format
101.result:
Observable Results:
 Part A
    Step 2: The NUT transmits a properly formatted Solicit message containing the following
    IA_PD option values:
         An option-code set to OPTION_IA_PD (25)
         An option-length set to 12 + length of IA_PD options field
         An IAID value set to a number
         Time T1 set to a number
         Time T2 set to a number
 Part B
    Step 4: The NUT transmits a properly formatted Solicit message.
    Step 6: The NUT transmits a properly formatted Request message containing the following
    Server Identifier option values:
         An option-code set to OPTION_SERVERID (2)
         An option-length set to length of DUID in octets
         DUID Field set to DUID for the Server
 Part C
    Step 9: The NUT transmits a properly formatted Request message containing the following
    IA_PD option values:
         An option-code set to OPTION_IA_PD (25)
         An option-length set to 12 + length of IA_PD options field
         An IAID value set to a number
         Time T1 set to a number
         Time T2 set to a number
         An IA_PD Prefix Option containing the following values:
         An option-code set to OPTION_IAPREFIX (26)
         An option-length set to 25 + length of Prefix options field
         A preferred lifetime and a valid lifetime
         A valid prefix length
         An IPv6 Prefix
 Part D
    Step 11: The NUT transmits a properly formatted Solicit message containing an IA_PD option.
    Step 14: The NUT transmits a properly formatted Solicit message containing an IA_PD with the same IAID as in step 7.

102.steps:
Part A: Valid Reply message in response to Request.
1. Enabled dhcpv6 in NUT, TR1 sets T1 to 50s and T2 to 80s.
2. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A and Link B.
3. Upon reception of a Renew message from the NUT at time T1.
4. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A and Link B.

Part B: Valid Reply message in response to a Renew message.
5. Enabled dhcpv6 in NUT, TR1 sets T1 to 50s and T2 to 80s.
6. The NUT should have received IPv6 prefix information from TR1. TR1 assigns the T1 and T2
parameters to the NUTĄŊs IA.
7. Upon reception of a Renew message from the NUT at time T1, TR1 transmits a properly
formatted Reply message.
8. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A and Link B.
9. After another T1 time elapse, NUT transmits a Renew message.
10. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A and Link B.

Part C: Valid Reply message in response to a Rebind message.
11. Enabled dhcpv6 in NUT, TR1 sets T1 to 50s and T2 to 80s.
12. The NUT should have received IPv6 address information from TR1. TR1 assigns the T1 and T2
parameters to the NUTĄŊs IA.
13. Upon reception of a Rebind message from the NUT at time T2, TR1 transmits a properly
formatted Reply message.
14. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A and Link B.
15. After another T1 time elapse, NUT transmits a Renew message.
16. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A and Link B.

Part D: Valid Reply message in response to a Release message.
17. Enabled dhcpv6 in NUT.
18. The NUT should have received IPv6 address information from TR1.
19. Configure NUT to release the IPv6 prefix.
20. Upon reception of the NUTĄŊs Release message, TR1 transmits a properly formatted Reply
message to the NUT.
21. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A and Link B.
102.title: To verify a DHCP requesting router device properly handles the reception of Reply messages during a basic message exchange
102.result:
Observable Results:

 Part A
    Step 2: The NUT should transmit a valid Request Message and TR1 transmit a valid Reply Message.
    Step 4: The NUT should send a valid Renew Message with the same prefix in the Reply message in step2.

 Part B
    Step 8: The NUT should send a valid Renew Message and TR1 transmit a valid Reply Message.
    Step 10: The NUT should send a valid Renew Message with the same prefix in the Reply message in step7.

 Part C
    Step 14: The NUT should send a valid Rebind Message and TR1 transmit a valid Reply.
    Step 16: The NUT should send a valid Renew Message with the same prefix in the Reply message in step13.

 Part D
    Step 21: The NUT should send a valid Release Message and TR1 transmit a valid Reply.

103.steps:
Part A: Multicast Addresses
    1. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT.

Part B: Valid UDP port
    3. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT.
    4. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.
    5. Upon reception of a Solicit message from the NUT, TN1 transmits an Advertise message to UDP port 546.
    6. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.

    7. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT.
    8. Upon reception of a Solicit message from the NUT, TN1 transmits an Advertise message to UDP destination port 33536.
    9. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.
103.title: To verify that the requesting router listens on the correct UDP port and transmits messages to the correct DHCP constant address
103.result:
Observable Results:
 Part A
    Step 1: The NUT must transmit a Solicit message with a destination address set to the Ą°ALL_DHCP_Relay_Agents_and_ServersĄą multicast address (FF02::1:2).

 Part B
    Step 4: The NUT must transmit a Solicit message with a destination UDP port set to 547.
    Step 6: The NUT must process the correct Advertise message and transmit a Request Message to TN1.

 Part C
    Step 9: The NUT should send a Destination Unreachable message to TN1 link-local address. The source address of the packet must be the NUT's unicast address. The code field must be set to "4" port unreachable and the invoking advertise packet included in the Error Message must not exceed minimum IPv6 MTU.

,

108.steps:
Part A: Solicit message format
1. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT.
2. Observe the first Solicit message transmitted on Link A.

,
Part B: Reliability of DHCPv6 Retransmission
3. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT.
4. Observe the first Solicit message transmitted on Link A.
5. Wait for second Solicit message.
6. Observe the second Solicit message transmitted on Link A.

,
Part C: Retransmission of Solicit Message
7. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT.
8. Observe the time the first Solicit message was transmitted on Link A.
9. Wait for second Solicit message.
10. Observe the time the second Solicit message was transmitted on Link A.

,
Part D: Maximum Retransmission Time of Solicit Message
11. Enable DHCPv6 on the NUT.
12. Continue to capture Solicit messages until RTprev= MRT + MRT*RAND (108 <= RTprev <=132).
13. Observe the messages transmitted on Link A.
14. Continue to capture Solicit messages until 776(0xffff+SOL_MAX_RT) seconds elapsed since the first Solicit message was received.
15. Observe the Elapsed Time Option in Solicit message transmitted on Link A.
108.title: To verify a requesting router device transmits properly formatted Solicit messages for Prefix Delegation.
108.result:
Part A
Step 2: The NUT transmits a properly formatted Solicit message containing the following elements:
 Src Address is a link-local for that interface
